s359:
This is a made-up story about a village market.

Mia went to the market on Saturday. A farmer had three heavy baskets of apples. Mia helped him carry them to his table.

She stayed to help for an hour. When she left, the farmer gave her two apples. She ate one and gave the other to a friend.

Next Saturday, Mia asked the farmer if he needed help again.
s360:
This is a made-up story about new neighbors.

A new family moved next door. Daniel wanted to talk to their son, Amir. They did not know many words in each other's language.

Daniel brought a ball outside. Amir smiled and came to play. They took turns kicking it.

After the game, they taught each other the word for ball. It was a small start. The next day, they played again.
s370:
Mr. Chen walked through the park on Sunday. He saw a small dog beside a bench. No one was with it.

He stayed a little way away and spoke softly. The dog came toward him. Its collar had a phone number on a small tag.

Mr. Chen called the number. Soon, a woman arrived. She was very happy to see her dog. She thanked him and took it home.
s382:
This story is made up. It is set long ago.

A river stood between a village and its market. People walked a long way to cross it. A builder named Thomas helped them make a wooden bridge.

The work took all summer. When the bridge was ready, the walk to the market was much shorter.

Years later, some wood needed replacing. The villagers worked together again to keep their bridge safe.
s383:
This story is made up. It is set long ago.

A family lived beside a lake. They grew food and kept animals. Each season brought different work.

In spring, they planted seeds. In summer, they cared for the plants. Before winter, they stored food.

During cold evenings, the family sat by the fire. Their grandmother told stories. The children listened while their parents repaired clothes for the next day.
s394:
Sleep gives our bodies time to rest. It also supports learning and memory.

After too little sleep, we may feel tired. Paying attention can be harder. Different people need different amounts of sleep. Age matters too.

A quiet bedtime routine can help us prepare for sleep. For example, we can put work away and read a little.

Sleep is part of everyday life, not time we have to earn by working hard.
s436:
This is a made-up story about a town meeting.

The town had money for one project. Some people wanted a new play area. Others wanted to fix the hall's roof. Water came through it when it rained.

The group chose to fix the roof first. People used the hall every week. They kept the play area on their list for next year.

Not everyone got their first choice, but everyone heard the reason.
s446:
Marta often lost a sock after washing her clothes. She looked behind the machine and under her bed. She found nothing.

One day, she moved the sofa to clean the floor. Several socks were underneath it. She picked them up and laughed.

Now she checks under the sofa when a sock is missing. Sometimes it is there. Sometimes she still has to look somewhere else.
s456:
This story is made up. It is set long ago.

A fire damaged three village homes. Everyone got out safely, but the families needed somewhere to stay. Their neighbors made space for them.

Over the following weeks, people helped repair the houses. Some brought wood. Others cooked meals for the workers.

The repairs took time. The families were glad that they did not have to do everything alone.
s506:
This is a made-up story about a city's buses.

The city offered free bus rides on one Saturday each month. Maria usually drove, but she decided to try the bus.

She found a stop near her home. The bus took her close to the shops. She did not have to find a parking space.

Maria began taking that bus more often. It suited this journey, though she still drove for some other trips.
s516:
Grandma kept her recipes on cards in a wooden box. Before a family meal, she chose a card and put it beside the stove.

Later, she gave the box to her daughter. Some cards were hard to read. Grandma helped explain the missing words.

Her daughter added new cards of her own. Now the box held recipes from both of them. They still used it when they cooked together.
s557:
Anton made shoes in a small shop. He often made an extra pair of little shoes. His neighbors asked who would wear them.

'Perhaps someone will need them,' he said.

One winter evening, a family came to the shop. Their child's shoes were worn out. One of Anton's spare pairs fitted well.

He gave the shoes to the family. The next morning, he began another small pair.
s597:
This is a made-up story about a town clean-up.

A few neighbors met once a month to pick up litter. They worked in the park for an hour. Then they stopped for a drink.

They invited other people to join. Some came often. Others helped when they had time.

The group kept the work short and the meeting place clear. This made it easier for new people to take part.
s842:
Dorothy is far from home. Her little dog, Toto, is with her. She walks along a yellow road.

She meets a man made of straw. He wants a brain. She meets a man made of tin. He wants a heart.

They all need help. They go along the road together. Dorothy has new friends now.
s843:
Black Beauty is a horse. He works hard for many owners. Some are kind. Some are not.

At last, he has a good home. A man there knows him from long ago. The man is glad to see him.

Black Beauty has food and rest. He does not need to leave again.
s857:
This story is set long ago. A road goes from a village to the sea.

A woman walks along it with a basket. She has eggs to sell. A man has cloth in his cart.

They stop by a well. Then they go on together. The market is not far now.
s1006:
Hana has a garden map. A new path is not on it.

She asks the gardener about the path. He says it is not ready yet. He is trying a new place for it.

Hana draws a light line on her map. She can change the line later. The garden is changing too.
s1016:
Pia sees a stone bird by a river. Its head faces the path. The next day, it faces the water.

Pia asks the gardener why. He says he turned it that morning.

He shows her a picture of the bird's old place. Now Pia knows what happened. She draws the bird in its new place.
s1326:
Theo is a made-up person. He helps at a theater. Some people cannot hear the actors.

Theo asks those people what would help. He works with a person who uses sign language. They plan with the actors.

More people can enjoy the next show. Theo keeps asking how to make it better.
s1466:
Mina sees a cup of water on a table. She does not know whose cup it is.

She puts a note beside it. The note asks who needs the water.

Her brother comes back. He says it is for a plant. He waters the plant and takes the cup away. Mina puts away her note.
s1467:
Ben has one red sock. The other sock is missing after the wash.

He looks in the machine. It is not there. He opens each shirt. Then he opens a big sheet.

The sock falls out. Ben puts the two socks together. He checks the sheet once more before he puts it away.
s1478:
A young man meets an old traveler. The traveler asks for food. The young man's brothers do not help.

The young man shares his food and drink. Later, he finds a golden goose with the traveler's help.

Other people want the gold. They touch the goose and cannot let go. They must follow the young man.|
s1489:
Luca finds a small blue stone. It sings when the wind blows.

He walks up a hill with the stone. There are more blue stones at the top. One place is empty.

Luca puts his stone there. The stones sing together. He sits and listens. Then the wind stops. Luca goes home with the song in his head.
s1490:
Nina finds a small cloud in a room. It wants to go outside. But it is afraid of the wind.

Nina opens the window. She holds a kite outside. The kite moves in the wind.

The cloud goes toward it. Soon, it is in the sky. Nina waves. The cloud waves back with a little rain.
s1501:
This story is set long ago. A woman makes pots. She wants a new bowl for small seeds.

She makes it from clay. She lets it dry. Then she fires it with care.

When it is cool, she puts seeds in it. The seeds stay inside. She makes a lid to keep the bowl closed.
s1521:
A small bird finds water by a path. It stays near the side.

It puts its head in the water. Then it shakes. Water goes over its back.

The bird comes out and sits in the sun. A person walks past slowly. The bird stays there for a little while. Then it flies away.
s1524:
A barn owl can hunt when there is little light. It uses its hearing as well as its eyes.

A mouse may be hard to see in long grass. Small sounds can help the owl find it.

The owl does not need to see every movement clearly. Information from its ears helps it search for food.
s1533:
Two children put ice in a bowl. The ice is hard and cold.

They leave the bowl on a table. Later, the ice is smaller. There is water around it.

They wait again. Now there is only water. The ice has not gone away. It has changed into water they can pour.
s1547:
This is a made-up story. Two school groups want the same field.

One group wants to run. The other wants to play ball. Both want to come after lunch.

The teachers talk together. One group comes first. The other comes later. On Friday, the groups play together. Now both groups have time on the field.
s1548:
This is a made-up story. A town has little water. Three streets share one water tank.

The families talk about what they need. They agree on times to get water. They check how much is left each day.

The rule helps them share. They still need more water. They ask the town for help.
s1549:
This is a made-up story about a library.

The library closed before many people came home from work. They asked for later hours. Keeping it open every evening would cost too much.

The staff tried two late evenings each week. More people could use the books and study tables.

After a month, the town checked the cost and the visits. It decided to keep those two evenings open.
s1722:
A desert tortoise lives in a dry place. It spends time in a home under the ground, away from great heat.

After rain, it can drink and store water in its body. This stored water matters when little water is available.

People should watch wild tortoises from a distance. Picking one up can disturb it and cause it to lose stored water.
